title: Polynomial-Time Serialization of Indexed Formula Concatenation
statement: Let $c$ assign a natural number to each bit string, and let $G(x,i)$ be a CNF formula over natural-number-indexed variables for each bit string $x$ and natural number $i$. If the function sending $x$ to the unary string of $c(x)$ ones is polynomial-time computable, and the function sending a pair encoding of bit strings $a,b$ to the fragment encoding of $G(a,|b|)$ is polynomial-time computable, then the function sending $x$ to the binary serialization of the CNF formula formed by concatenating $G(x,i)$ for all $i$ with $0\le i<c(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A function from bit strings to natural numbers, $c$.
A function from a bit string and a natural number to CNF formulas, $G$.
The unary encoding of $c(x)$ is polynomial-time computable.
The function mapping a pair encoding of $a,b$ to the fragment encoding of $G(a,|b|)$ is polynomial-time computable.
